description:
About the Job:

Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.

As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”

Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.

This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

  • Product & Value
    • Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.
    • Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.
    • Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.
    • Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.
  • Change & Adoption
    • Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.
    • Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.
  • Executive & Growth
    • Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.
    • Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.
  • Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)
    • Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.
  • Delivery & Execution
    • Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.
    • Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-projection early; partner with PM-type support (where it exists on an account) for detailed tracking and change-order mechanics.
  • Customer Landscape
    • Our customers struggle with long lead times, risky deployments, feature flag sprawl, unclear ownership of releases, and a gap between what engineering ships and what the business expects. You’ll need to speak confidently about CI/CD, progressive delivery, testing and quality gates, how agent-generated changes affect release risk, and delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. You don’t need to write the code. You do need to know when a customer is describing a real constraint and when they’re describing a habit.

Qualifications:

  • Core
    • 8+ years of relevant experience, ideally in senior, client-facing roles across product management, delivery, or consulting within B2B SaaS or technology services; or as a forward-deployed/deployment strategist, or early builder/founder at a high-growth tech startup.
    • Product and systems thinking: you can define what to deliver and why (MVP or first-phase scoping, prioritization, and success criteria) and manage scope against it.
    • Value-based scoping experience (ROI/TCO) with executive buyers, ideally within sales cycles.
    • A track record owning both delivery accountability and the executive relationship on the same engagement, with the judgment to decide whether an engagement’s scope still serves the business, not just execute against an agreed plan. Executive-level communication and presence.
    • You’ve helped an organization move off an entrenched process and adopt a new way of working, not just documented a better one, including facilitating workshops with mixed engineering and leadership groups and adapting formats on the fly.
    • Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, with good judgment about their limits.
    • Enough confidence in SDLC and software delivery to be credible with technical stakeholders, and experience partnering closely with technical roles (solutions engineers, architects, or similar).
  • Preferred Qualifications
    • Familiarity with progressive delivery and feature management, ideally including LaunchDarkly or a similar tool. Fluency with delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. We’ll teach you the LaunchDarkly specifics.
    • Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.
    • Experience writing PRDs and managing agile software projects.
    • Experience surfacing expansion/renewal signals to Sales or AM; comfort with a role that may take on commercial ownership over time.
    • (Bonus) Experience operating in a scaling PS org where role boundaries are still being defined.

Travel

  • Travel roughly once per quarter for customer workshops and team onsites; more frequent travel may be needed around specific engagements.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level P4:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $171,200- $235,400**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $154,100 - $211,860**
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $145,500 - $200,090**

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. 

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability
